public_rationale: The contemporary official documentation describes Playwright as a testing and automation framework, with browser actions specified through code. That supports the claim about Playwright scripting itself. It does not support a broader inference that an application using Playwright cannot also contain AI.
limitations: The assessment follows the immediate antecedent and supplied normalized proposition.
This evidence does not determine how Rabbit generated or selected its scripts.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The Playwright scripting Rabbit uses is not AI.

statement.excerpt: Like I said, useful. But it isn’t AI.

our_interpretation: The immediate antecedent of it is Playwright and its scripted browser actions, matching the supplied normalized proposition.
The ordinary reading is that the automation framework itself is not an AI model. This does not establish whether Rabbit used AI to create, select or control scripts.
Use the framework available during the launch period through May 13. Versioned documentation avoids importing later capabilities.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous official documentation describes ordinary programmed browser automation and demonstrates actions executed through explicit API calls rather than an AI model.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous implementation evidence shows that the framework's relevant browser-action mechanism itself performs AI inference, rather than receiving instructions from separately supplied code.
